findings.title: Art Style Disconnect
findings.where: Title screen, compared to all other screens.
findings.problem: The title screen uses a high-detail, painterly/photorealistic illustration. The in-game art style is a top-down, low-resolution aesthetic with pixel art elements.
findings.why: This creates a jarring disconnect and sets false expectations for the game's visual style. It makes the project feel like it's using placeholder art and lacks a cohesive visual identity from the very first impression.
findings.fix: Replace the title screen background with 'key art' illustrated in the same top-down, pixel-art style as the game itself. This could be a more dramatic, composed scene (e.g., the player's vehicle in a garage, or facing off against an enemy in the city) that accurately represents the game's look and feel.

findings.title: Abstract Constructor Schematic
findings.where: Constructor screen, the 'SUBCOMPACT - TOP VIEW' panel on the right.
findings.problem: The vehicle schematic is a simple, abstract blue outline with two rectangles inside. It provides no visual information about the selected parts or the final appearance of the car.
findings.why: This fails to visually connect the player's choices to the vehicle they are building, which is a core fantasy of the game. It makes the building process feel like a spreadsheet and robs the player of the satisfaction of seeing their creation come together.
findings.fix: Replace the abstract schematic with a preview using the actual in-game vehicle sprite. As the player selects different chassis, armor, and weapons from the list on the left, update the sprite preview in real-time to show those parts being added or changed.

findings.title: Ambiguous City Icons
findings.where: City screen, the icons floating above the buildings.
findings.problem: The icons are colored chevrons (green, blue, orange) pointing up or down. Their meaning is not intuitive from the design alone.
findings.why: This forces the player to guess or memorize what each icon represents, hindering their ability to make strategic decisions about where to go. It adds unnecessary cognitive load and makes navigating the city confusing.
findings.fix: Replace the abstract chevrons with simple, recognizable pictograms. For example: a wrench for a garage, a shopping cart for a market, a target reticle for an arena, and a briefcase for jobs. Use color primarily to denote status (e.g., green for available, grey for unavailable) rather than type.

findings.title: Illegible Condition Panel
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, the 'CONDITION' panel on the right.
findings.problem: The panel uses small text and low-contrast indicators. The minus-sign icons for missing armor plates are difficult to distinguish from the empty slots at a glance. All health bars are the same green color.
findings.why: During high-speed combat, the player needs to assess their vehicle's status instantly. This panel's poor legibility makes that impossible, forcing them to take their eyes off the action to read, which can lead to frustrating mistakes.
findings.fix: Increase the contrast and clarity. Replace the faint '-' icons for missing armor with brightly colored, empty red brackets `[ ]` and use a solid green block `■` for intact armor. Use a traffic-light color system for the health bars: green for >75%, yellow for 25-75%, and red for <25% health.

findings.title: Monotonous Ground Textures
findings.where: City, Arena, and Road screens; the ground surfaces.
findings.problem: The ground is covered in a single, repetitive, noisy texture (cracked concrete, asphalt, or dirt). It lacks variation, large-scale detail, or handcrafted elements.
findings.why: This makes the game world feel flat, artificial, and visually boring. It lacks a sense of place and atmosphere. On the Road screen, the lack of variation also makes it harder to judge speed.
findings.fix: Break up the tiling by creating larger texture variations and blending between them. Add decals like oil stains, tire marks, larger unique crack patterns, painted lines (parking spaces, faded lane markings), and small debris sprites to create visual interest and a sense of history.
